aboutParagraphs: Technip Hughes manages buildings across Qatar, from MEP and fire safety to cleaning, security, pools and landscaping. Its buyers are building owners, property managers and procurement teams who compare FM providers carefully before signing a long contract.

Technip Hughes is a Doha-based facility management company with more than a decade of operational experience. It positions itself as a single accountable partner: one account manager, one help desk and one invoice for every service a building needs.

It runs CAFM-based, data-driven maintenance, plans around Qatar's summer heat and dust, and aligns energy efficiency with Qatar National Vision 2030. Its services cover integrated FM, MEP maintenance, soft FM, fire safety, security, pools and landscaping, for commercial offices, residential, hospitality and retail, government and education, and industrial sites.
challengeLead: Three problems shaped the design brief.

challenges.title: Six services that must feel like one partner
challenges.description: MEP, cleaning, fire safety, security and landscaping are often bought from different vendors. The site had to show each service clearly while selling the idea of one integrated provider.

challenges.title: A high-value, low-frequency purchase
challenges.description: FM contracts are long and expensive. Buyers research for weeks and compare several providers, so the site had to build confidence and give them an easy, low-risk next step.

challenges.title: Standing out in a crowded Qatar market
challenges.description: Many FM companies in Doha look the same online. Technip Hughes needed a premium look and a clear message to be remembered on the shortlist.

objectiveLead: Design a premium, fast and mobile-friendly facility management website that explains six services and five sectors clearly, proves experience with real numbers, and turns visits into proposal requests by phone, WhatsApp and the enquiry form.
objectives: Explain six services and five sectors clearly
Turn visits into proposal requests by phone, WhatsApp and the enquiry form
approachLead: Five design pillars, plus a homepage ordered like a sales conversation.

approachPillars.title: A premium, restrained look
paragraphs: We used a deep teal palette, full-width photography of real building types and a formal, confident tone. The result feels like a corporate partner, not a cleaning contractor, which matches the value of an FM contract.

approachPillars.title: Clear structure for services and sectors
paragraphs: The main menu has dropdowns for each service. The homepage shows six service cards that link to detail pages, and five sector cards with images for offices, residences, hospitality and retail, government and industrial sites.

approachPillars.title: Proof before the pitch
paragraphs: A stats bar under the hero shows 10+ years, 2,000+ clients, 200+ professionals and 6+ markets. "The Technip Hughes Advantage" sets out five principles, followed by quality and safety standards, a portfolio and a client section.

approachPillars.title: Easy, low-risk enquiries
paragraphs: A top bar shows office hours with call and WhatsApp links. "Get an Estimate" stays in the header, "Request a Proposal" opens a prefilled WhatsApp message, and a four-step approach explains that a site assessment comes before any commitment.

approachPillars.title: Speed, accessibility and SEO
paragraphs: Built with Astro, the site ships very little JavaScript, so pages load fast on mobile. Images are WebP, there is a skip-to-content link, one H1 with clear H2 and H3 headings, descriptive link text and a six-question FAQ.

approachPillars.title: How the homepage guides a buyer
paragraphs: We ordered the homepage like a sales conversation, so each section answers the next question a buyer has. Because every section ends close to a call or WhatsApp button, a buyer can act the moment they feel ready.
Hero with H1 and two CTAs: Is this an FM company in Qatar, and how do I contact them?
Stats bar: Are they big and experienced enough?
About and six service cards: Can they handle everything my building needs?
Technip Hughes Advantage: Why choose them over other FM companies?
Sectors: Do they work with buildings like mine?
Four-step approach: What happens after I get in touch?
Quality, portfolio and clients: Can I trust their standards and track record?
Coverage and FAQ: Do they cover my area, and what will it cost?
Contact section: How do I request a proposal now?

whyMattersHeading: Why design matters for facility management in Qatar
whyMattersParagraphs: An FM company is trusted with a building's safety, comfort and running costs. Buyers judge that trust first by the website. A dated or confusing site quietly removes a provider from the shortlist.

With a premium look, clear services, real proof and easy enquiries, Technip Hughes now has a website that works like its best account manager. That is what a strong web design company in Qatar should deliver.

Next for the website: move from the Vercel preview address to the final company domain, add descriptive alt text to all photos, create a dedicated page for each sector, and add an Arabic version for Arabic-speaking decision makers.

faqs.question: What should a facility management website include?
faqs.answer: Clear service pages, sectors served, proof such as years, clients and team size, safety standards, a portfolio, FAQs and easy contact by phone, WhatsApp and form.

faqs.question: Why use Astro for a company website?
faqs.answer: Astro sends very little JavaScript to the browser, so pages load fast. Speed helps both user experience and Google rankings, especially on mobile.

faqs.question: Why add a prefilled WhatsApp message to a website?
faqs.answer: It saves the visitor from typing and starts the conversation instantly. In Qatar, many buyers prefer WhatsApp for first contact.

faqs.question: Can Teknoppy build bilingual English and Arabic websites?
faqs.answer: Yes. Teknoppy builds multilingual websites and can add an Arabic version with right-to-left layout.

faqs.question: How long does a corporate website project take?
faqs.answer: It depends on pages, content and integrations. Teknoppy gives a written timeline and fixed quote after a free consultation.

faqs.question: Does Teknoppy design websites for businesses in Qatar?
faqs.answer: Yes. Teknoppy is a web design and SEO company in Kochi, Kerala, building websites for clients in Qatar, the UAE and across the GCC.
